title: SharePoint: automatically archive inactive files with an Advanced Management policy
summary: The briefing's controls, opt-in default and licensing and billing statements are supported by Microsoft documentation. It correctly reports the roadmap targets and flags the documented differences in default thresholds and OneDrive scope.

claims.claim: New-SPOFileArchivePolicy -PolicyType SelectedSites -LastAccessDateCriteria 12 creates a selected-sites policy with a 12-month inactivity criterion.
claims.quote: New-SPOFileArchivePolicy -PolicyType "SelectedSites" -Name "ArchiveMarketing" -LastAccessDateCriteria 12

claims.claim: Set-SPOFileArchivePolicy -PolicyId <policy GUID> -State Active activates the identified policy.
claims.quote:
Set-SPOFileArchivePolicy -PolicyId "a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-abcd-ef1234567890" -State "Active"

claims.claim: Set-SPOFileArchivePolicy -PolicyId <policy GUID> -IsWhatIfMode $false selects enforcement for the identified policy.
claims.quote:
-PolicyId <Guid> ... [-IsWhatIfMode <Boolean>]
When set to `$false`, the policy archives files normally when active.

claims.claim: Add-SPOSiteToFileArchivePolicy -PolicyId <policy GUID> -Site <site URL> -Exclude adds a site exclusion to the identified policy.
claims.quote:
Add-SPOSiteToFileArchivePolicy
    -PolicyId <Guid>
    -Site <SpoSitePipeBind>
    [-Exclude]
Adds the site as an exclusion instead of an inclusion, exempting it from the policy when the policy runs.

claims.claim: Get-SPOFileArchivePolicyReport -PolicyId <policy GUID> retrieves run reports for the identified policy.
claims.quote:
Get-SPOFileArchivePolicyReport
    -PolicyId <Guid>
This cmdlet retrieves the run reports for a file archive policy.

claims.quote: Specifies the number of months since a file was last accessed before it becomes eligible for archiving. Valid values range from 6 to 48.

claims.where: summary; front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Scope
claims.claim: Microsoft 365 Archive follows a pay-as-you-go billing model.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 Archive follows a pay-as-you-go model, and is configured through the Microsoft 365 admin center.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Archive storage is billed per GB archived on a monthly basis.
claims.quote: Storage consumption is charged at a per-GB monthly rate.

claims.where: Why it matters; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Archive storage charges apply only when combined archived and active SharePoint storage exceeds the tenant's included or licensed capacity.
claims.quote: This meter is charged only when archived storage plus active storage in SharePoint exceeds the included or licensed allocated SharePoint storage capacity limit of the tenant.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The pricing page's billing examples use $0.05/GB/month.
claims.quote: Pay at $0.05/GB/month for 200 GB of archive storage.

claims.claim: The Archive pricing page points to Pay-as-you-go services and pricing for pricing.
claims.quote: To see the pricing for Microsoft 365 Archive, see Pay-as-you-go services and pricing.

claims.claim: Monthly archive usage includes storage used by archived SharePoint sites.
claims.quote: Monthly archive storage usage is calculated as the total of two components: (1) the storage used by all archived SharePoint sites, and (2) the storage used by archived files that reside in non-archived SharePoint sites.

claims.claim: Monthly archive usage also includes archived files in non-archived SharePoint sites.
claims.quote: Monthly archive storage usage is calculated as the total of two components: (1) the storage used by all archived SharePoint sites, and (2) the storage used by archived files that reside in non-archived SharePoint sites.

claims.claim: Archived content remains archived when Archive is turned off or billing is unhealthy.
claims.quote: If Microsoft 365 Archive is turned off, or if the associated archive billing subscription is unhealthy or turned off, archived content stays archived.

claims.claim: Archived content can still be reactivated when Archive or billing is unavailable.
claims.quote: Archived content can still be reactivated.

claims.claim: New archive actions are blocked until Archive is enabled and billing is healthy.
claims.quote: New archive actions are blocked until Microsoft 365 Archive is turned on and billing is healthy.

claims.claim: Archived content counts as active storage while Archive or billing is unavailable.
claims.quote: While Microsoft 365 Archive or billing is unavailable, archived content counts as active storage usage and counts toward standard Microsoft 365 storage consumption.

claims.claim: OneDrive sites are not supported in the policy preview described by the feature page.
claims.quote: OneDrive sites aren't supported in this preview. Use a SharePoint site for your pilot.

claims.claim: The New-SPOFileArchivePolicy reference nevertheless lists AllODBSites as a policy type for OneDrive for Business.
claims.quote: AllODBSites: The policy applies to all OneDrive for Business sites in the tenant.

claims.claim: The required PowerShell module is Microsoft.Online.SharePoint.PowerShell version 16.0.27709.12000 or later.
claims.quote: You're using Microsoft.Online.SharePoint.PowerShell version 16.0.27709.12000 or later.

claims.claim: A policy can hold at most 1,000 associated sites, counting inclusions or exclusions rather than the entire AllSites scope.
claims.quote: A single policy can contain a maximum of 1,000 associated sites. For SelectedSites policies, those associations are inclusions. For AllSites policies, those associations are exclusions.

claims.claim: Each AllSites policy run scans at most 100,000 sites during preview.
claims.quote: Sites scanned per AllSites policy run | 100,000 sites | Hard limit per run

claims.claim: Remaining AllSites sites are scanned in subsequent monthly runs.
claims.quote: The policy continues scanning remaining sites in subsequent monthly runs. Evaluating all eligible sites can therefore require more than one monthly run.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans to increase the AllSites scan limit to 1,000,000 sites per run by general availability.
claims.quote: Microsoft plans to increase the AllSites scan limit to 1,000,000 sites per run by general availability.

claims.claim: Built-in file type exclusions apply regardless of the policy's file type filters.
claims.quote: These exclusions apply regardless of the file type filters configured for the policy.

claims.claim: OneNote files cannot be archived.
claims.quote: Certain file types can't be archived, including OneNote, SharePoint pages, and SharePoint agents.

claims.claim: SharePoint pages cannot be archived.
claims.quote: Certain file types can't be archived, including OneNote, SharePoint pages, and SharePoint agents.

claims.claim: SharePoint agents cannot be archived.
claims.quote: Certain file types can't be archived, including OneNote, SharePoint pages, and SharePoint agents.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 Archive must be set up with pay-as-you-go billing in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
claims.quote:
Microsoft 365 Archive follows a pay-as-you-go model, and is configured through the Microsoft 365 admin center.
Before you can use Microsoft 365 Archive, you must first link your Azure subscription in pay-as-you-go billing.

claims.claim: Enabling Archive alone does not create an inactive files policy.
claims.quote: The current preview requires SharePoint Advanced Management entitlement and PowerShell configuration; enabling Archive alone doesn't create a policy.

claims.claim: -Exclude is valid only for AllSites or AllODBSites policies.
claims.quote: Exclusions are only valid for a policy whose PolicyType is `AllSites` or `AllODBSites`. Adding an exclusion to a `SelectedSites` policy returns an error.

claims.claim: Omitting -Exclude adds an inclusion, which is valid only for SelectedSites policies.
claims.quote: By default, the site is added as an inclusion. Inclusions are only valid for a policy whose PolicyType is `SelectedSites`

claims.claim: Policy run reports are available for the past 12 months.
claims.quote: Reports are kept for the past 12 months and include details about each policy run such as how many sites were processed, how many files were archived, and the total storage archived.

claims.claim: The report command is read-only and does not change the policy.
claims.quote: This cmdlet retrieves the run reports for a file archive policy.

claims.claim: A SelectedSites policy needs at least one included site before activation.
claims.quote: To activate a `SelectedSites` policy, at least one site must have been added as an inclusion using `Add-SPOSiteToFileArchivePolicy` without `-Exclude`. Excluded sites don't satisfy this requirement.

claims.claim: For policies covering more than 100,000 sites, Microsoft directs administrators to create a new policy with the same criteria and scope and set IsWhatIfMode $false on that new policy.
claims.quote: If your policy covers more than 100,000 sites, create a new policy with the same criteria, scope, and site inclusions or exclusions when you're ready to archive files. Set `IsWhatIfMode` to `$false` on the new policy.

claims.claim: Switching the existing simulation policy to archiving resumes its previous processing position and may skip sites already evaluated in simulation.
claims.quote: Switching the existing simulation policy to archiving resumes from its previous processing position instead of starting over, so sites already evaluated in simulation might be skipped.

claims.claim: The New-SPOFileArchivePolicy reference states that an omitted -LastAccessDateCriteria results in an 18-month service threshold.
claims.quote: This parameter has no PowerShell-side default. When omitted, the service applies an inactivity threshold of 18 months to the new policy.

claims.claim: The feature page instead states a 24-month default inactivity threshold.
claims.quote: The policy commands accept an inactivity threshold from 6 through 48 months. The default is 24 months.

claims.claim: Manual file archiving is a separate control, and disabling the user-facing Archive action does not prevent automatic policy archiving.
claims.quote: Manual file archiving and automatic policy archiving are separate controls. Disabling the user-facing Archive action doesn't prevent automatic policies from archiving files.

claims.claim: The file archive policy cmdlet references mark the feature as currently in preview.
claims.quote: This cmdlet is part of the file archive policies feature which is currently in preview.

claims.claim: Policy reports provide simulation or enforcement run results for reviewing processing coverage and archive impact.
claims.quote: Reports are kept for the past 12 months and include details about each policy run such as how many sites were processed, how many files were archived, and the total storage archived.
